goldens.comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully

The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts:125 — The async forEach is never awaited, so calendar deletion can outlive the reschedule response and its import/delete rejection bypasses the surrounding catch.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that on line 125, `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {` is used with an async callback. The forEach method does not await the promises returned by async callbacks, meaning the calendar deletion operations (line 128: `const calendar = await getCalendar(...)` and the subsequent `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)`) will execute without being awaited. This means: 1) The surrounding try-catch block won't catch any rejections from these async operations, 2) The function can return before the deletions complete, and 3) Any errors in the deletion process will be unhandled promise rejections. This is a real bug introduced by the change from synchronous to asynchronous getCalendar.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at lines 457-475 in handleCancelBooking.ts, the code uses `.forEach(async (credential) => {...})` which creates async callbacks that are not awaited. The `apiDeletes.push()` calls inside these async callbacks will execute after the forEach completes, meaning the promises won't be added to `apiDeletes` before the later `Promise.all(apiDeletes)` runs. This is a real race condition bug where calendar deletions for recurring events may be skipped because the promises aren't collected properly.

This changes the entire module loading pattern across multiple files. The finding correctly identifies that there are no tests covering this new async loading behavior. While the code changes are visible in the diff (packages/app-store/index.ts converting all imports to dynamic import() calls), there are no test file changes included.
